images.title: Top number against bottom
images.purpose: Show that when the numerator is bigger than the denominator the amount is more than one whole, and when it is smaller the amount is less than one.
images.composition: Two groups of tall glasses with a wide gap between them: two glasses on the left, one glass on the right, each group with its fraction and comparison underneath.
images.exact_structure: Three identical tall straight-sided glasses, each split by thin grey #6B7280 lines into exactly 5 equal horizontal parts. Left group: first glass with all 5 parts filled teal #0072B2; second glass with only the bottom 1 part filled amber #E69F00, 4 parts empty. Right group, set well apart: one glass with the bottom 4 parts filled teal and the top 1 part empty. Exactly 3 glasses, 15 parts, 10 filled.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: Numerator bigger than denominator means more than one whole.
images.description: Left: one full glass of 5 fifths and a second glass with 1 fifth, labelled 6/5, 6 > 5, more than 1 glass. Right: one glass with 4 fifths, labelled 4/5, 4 < 5, less than 1 glass.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to compare the top and bottom numbers in each fraction and say which group goes past one glass.

image_decisions.why: Glasses in fifths make it visible why a bigger top number goes past one whole.
